question.text: A particle is in motion along a curve $12 y=x^{3}$. The rate of change of its ordinate exceeds that of abscissa in

solution.text:
Given, curve, $12 y=x^{3}$
and $\frac{d y}{d t}>\frac{d x}{d t}$ ....(i)
Now, $12 \frac{d y}{d t}=3 x^{2} \frac{d x}{d t}$....(ii)
From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$\Rightarrow$
$$
\begin{aligned}
3 x^{2} \frac{d x}{d t} &>12 \frac{d x}{d t} \\
3 x^{2} &>12
\end{aligned}
$$
$\Rightarrow \quad x^{2}-4>0$
$\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & (x-2)(x+2)>0 \\ \Rightarrow & x \in(-\infty,-2) \cup(2, \infty)\end{array}$
